mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the last two months indicates a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST shows a sustained increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to increased wages and consumer spending, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last month signals increased economic activity and supply-side growth, which is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over the last quarter, it indicates a shift in demand composition towards consumption, which is a strong driver of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the last month indicates a robust labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over the last two months signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL shows a sustained increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real GDP (GDPC1) over the last quarter, coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the last month, signals a weakening economy, which is negatively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decrease and UNRATE increase in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.
